title: [Model] Optimize Qwen3-TTS streaming throughput and first audio on CUDA
body:
## Purpose

Improve Qwen3-TTS streaming throughput and first-audio latency on a single CUDA GPU. The experimental single-GPU profile combines frame-local residual-predictor KV reuse, supplied-uniform fused sampling, time-major codec convolutions, scoped cuDNN autotuning, and eager residual prediction with first-frame delivery from the Talker.

The Talker can send the first frame without a stage hop. Code2Wav advances its causal state without emitting that frame again; explicit per-request metadata and output ordering preserve the first frame ahead of subsequent codec chunks, including when the final codec output arrives first. Reference-code requests and unsupported runners/platforms retain regular codec delivery. Qwen3-TTS profiles explicitly request first-audio delivery; it activates only for CUDA MRV2, async chunks, TP/PP 1, an in-process executor, and disabled prefix caching.

title: [Bugfix] Fix MiniCPM-o 4.5 seeded turns and window E2E inputs
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #8154.

Seeded MiniCPM-o 4.5 duplex requests fail with missing `response.done` and listen-only events. After #8152, the seed is marked pending, but its prompt opens an assistant turn while initialization still leaves `current_turn_ended=True`. Seeded plain-text requests can consequently remain listen-only. Initialize the existing native turn state with the seeded prefix and retain pending input through `tts_bos`, consuming it on the first content token. The model's `turn_eos` still closes the response and later silence returns to normal listening.

The short-window tests have a separate input problem: they discard context before retaining a complete 5.47-second fixture utterance, then stop the audio clock immediately after speech. The same input produced only listen decisions with windowing **disabled**. Retain enough context and send a five-second pause before commit. Basic and context windows still rebuild; completion, audio, error, close, subsequent-session, burst-input, camera, and two-minute-input assertions are unchanged.

Add a seed lifecycle regression covering absent/empty/English/Chinese text, speech-envelope handling, and silence after `turn_eos`.

title: [BugFix][Cosmos3] Decode uploaded video paths in v2v preprocess
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #8073.

Nightly Diffusion X2V 2-GPU perf failed on `test_cosmos3_v2v_official_demo_2gpu-1280x720_frames189_steps4` with `AssertionError: Request failures exist` (3/3 requests). Same step **t2i / t2v / i2v passed**. This is a deterministic v2v input-path bug, not a timeout and not #7912 (`no_guardrails`).

## Root cause

Video serving persists multipart uploads as `/tmp/vllm_omni_video_reference_*.mp4` and puts that **path list** in `multi_modal_data["video"]` (the API keeps file paths for models that need the source file).

Cosmos3 `pre_process_func` then:

1. `_video_payload_to_frames()` saw a `list` and returned it unchanged.
2. With no image, it took `raw_video_frames[0]` (the `.mp4` path) through `_pil_to_rgb`.
3. `_pil_to_rgb` treated `str` as an image and called `PIL.Image.open(path)`.

PIL cannot open mp4 → `UnidentifiedImageError: cannot identify image file '/tmp/vllm_omni_video_reference_….mp4'`.

Decoded PIL frame lists (existing unit tests) already worked. The nightly v2v client goes through the upload/path path, so only v2v failed.

title: [Bugfix][Diffusion] Skip AllGather DLO weight restore on worker shutdown
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #8081.

**What broke:** after successful generation, closing a pipeline that uses AllGather DLO left diffusion workers in cleanup. After the 15 s `_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S`, the executor sent SIGTERM (logged as `SystemExit: 143` inside `restore_tensor_storage(..., device="cpu")`), then SIGKILL. The run also logged a 30 s orchestrator timeout and leaked semaphores.

title: [Core][Diffusion] Add byte backpressure to chunk transfers
body:
## Summary

Part of #6872.

```diff
 VAE chunk -> uint8 preparation -> pinned D2H ring -> MP4 encoder
-                              admit while a slot is free
+                              admit while a slot is free
+                                and pending bytes stay <= 256 MiB
```

The existing two-slot ring bounded chunk count, but its memory footprint still
scaled with resolution, batch size, and chunk length. This adds byte-aware
admission to the same ring: hitting either the slot or byte limit propagates
backpressure to the VAE producer.

A native chunk larger than the byte budget may proceed only when the ring is
otherwise empty, avoiding a permanent wait for legal chunk shapes. Reservations
are made under the ring lock and released with the slot's final reader. The
session drains its oldest in-flight lease before waiting so byte pressure cannot
self-deadlock.

## Evidence

- **Before:** admission checked only for a free slot; two variable-sized chunks
  could both enter the ring regardless of their combined bytes.
- **After:** focused tests cover byte-pressure waits with free slots, atomic byte
  accounting, oversized single-chunk progress, oldest-first session drainin

title: [Bugfix] Avoid waveform-list GC scans and release completed MOSS batches
body:
## Purpose

Warming many reference voices leaves decoded waveforms in the API server as large Python float lists. A full GC must traverse their element references even when the waveforms are live and no garbage is collected. MOSS's idle reference-encoder drainer also retains its completed `first`/`jobs` batch while awaiting the next queue item; subsequent speaker-code cache hits may never supply that next item.

This change:

- Stores owned, C-contiguous float32 arrays in the shared waveform LRU and accounts for numeric storage with `nbytes`.
- Gives MOSS reference encoding an array resolver. Existing list-based consumers, including MOSS Nano's IPC payload, retain the list interface through a temporary conversion; no second list cache is retained.

## [Bugfix] Drain the omni connector output on the main thread in the AR runner

Qwen3-Omni-MoE hangs on XPU during decode with async scheduling and TP > 1.

### Cause

`get_omni_connector_output()` broadcasts from rank 0 over the TP group's shared-memory ring when `async_chunk` is on and TP > 1. 
`GPUARModelRunner.sample_tokens` called it inside the deferred`output_builder()` closure, which async scheduling runs on a background thread,while `execute_model()` broadcasts on the same group from the main thread. 
The broadcast order then differs per rank, and the ring pairs messages positionally, so it skews permanently and every rank blocks:

```
INFO [shm_broadcast.py:801] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds.
```

### Fix

Drain the connector on the main thread and attach the result to the built output, leaving no collectives on the builder thread. This matches `gpu_generation_model_runner`, `npu_generation_model_runner` and `npu_ar_model_runner`, which already drain on the main thread, the GPU AR runner was the only one that deferred it.

## Purpose Add cross-request prefix caching for the HunyuanImage3 single DiT stage. body:
## Purpose

Fixes #7684.

Diffusion stages have worker-level sleep/wake but no scheduler-level pause: `AsyncOmni.pause_generation` only closes frontend admission for them, `DiffusionEngine` keeps scheduling whatever is queued, and the only way to make a busy replica quiet before a sleep or a weight update is to abort everything, which discards batches that have already executed.

This adds `pause_generation(mode="keep")` for diffusion stages running request-level execution:

- `DiffusionEngine` answers `pause_scheduler(mode="keep")` / `resume_scheduler` itself (queued, async and bootstrap entry points). title: [LingBot World] Shard the streaming VAE decode across the Ulysses ranks
body:
## Purpose

Shard the LingBot-World streaming VAE decode across the Ulysses ranks along the width, using the existing halo-exchanging Wan decoder shard. No new option: a multi-rank deployment is what asks for it.

The DiT already runs on `sequence_parallel_size` ranks, and until now each of them decoded the whole frame so that its own `post_decode` could carry on. With the shard each rank decodes a quarter of it (at four ranks) and every rank keeps the assembled frame, because the gather is an all-gather anyway. The streaming decoder composes with it as is (`feat_cache`, `feat_idx`, `first_chunk` pass straight through to the patched decoder) and the per-session temporal cache shrinks by the same factor (1801 -> 450 MiB per rank at 480x832).

`vae_patch_parallel_size` stays rejected for this pipeline, as before: it would make the registry force tiling and set up the tiled distributed executor underneath a decoder that is already sharded.
